function: Deterministic, non-model check that reads the emitted learner-facing document (document/<UNIT>.md) immediately after runtime/session_bridge.py:_markdown() writes it and before the PDF is built. Asserts that no learner-facing section body parses as JSON, that no line matches a serialized-object signature (a line that is exactly '{', '[', or a leading-whitespace '"key":' pair), that every section named in the prose contract inputs/unit_prose.v1.md is present as prose, and that the document contains no residual template placeholder. Emits a DOC-RENDER-CONFORMANCE verdict into results/unit_checks.json naming the offending file and line, and blocks the transition to LAB_PDF on failure so no PDF, no page render and no reviewer cycle is ever spent on an unreadable document.
what_makes_it_sota: Current practice assigns exactly this class of property to deterministic code rather than to a model reviewer: Braintrust (26 February 2026) states 'Deterministic checks should handle everything that can be measured directly, including format, schema compliance, and required fields', and Agents' Last Exam (arXiv:2606.05405) 'deliberately avoids LLM-as-judge wherever a deterministic alternative exists'. Treating realization as a checkable stage rather than a formatting detail follows the NLG field's own division of labour, where surface realization is separately benchmarked (2018 Surface Realization shared task, arXiv:1805.07731). The specific check is engineering rather than a published result, and no source in this scan studies this exact defect.
role_in_curriculum_builder: New deterministic check in the gate-2 family (DOC-*), invoked inside runtime/session_bridge.py:finalize() between the markdown write at line 269 and the pandoc PDF render at line 271, and recorded in results/unit_checks.json alongside LAB-SCHEMA-VALID. Blocking. It runs before ARTIFACT_CONSISTENCY, QA_COMMUNICATION, LAB_PDF, PDF_RENDER and PDF_VISUAL_QA in policy/controller.v1.yaml, so it is the earliest possible point at which the defect is visible.
issues_resolved: The defect that prompted this scan: 'Document renderer dumps raw JSON as lesson body. All 4 lessons (L01-L04). Sections under "Engage/Explore/Explain/..." contain literal structured objects instead of prose' (QA report, Critical). Root cause confirmed in code at runtime/session_bridge.py:207-215, where eight sections are emitted via json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2). Every executed check passed anyway, because results/unit_checks.json contains only schema, verifier and receipt checks, all of which correctly describe an upstream lab.json that was never the problem.

function: Deterministic reviewer that runs a readability formula battery (FKGL plus corroborating indices such as ARI, SMOG and Gunning Fog) and a new-term counter over the rendered document text, compares both against the band declared in the unit's calibration.yaml, and emits TEXT-READABILITY-BAND and TEXT-BLOOM-VERBS verdicts. Counts terms introduced in the document body against the declared vocabulary list in workers/lab.json and fails when the body introduces undefined terms beyond the cap. Blocks on the readability band; TEXT-BLOOM-VERBS flags and records without blocking, per the existing prompt.md gate-2 definition.
what_makes_it_sota: The metric battery is standard and model-free: Zhang et al., Frontiers in Public Health (20 February 2026), evaluate LLM-generated educational text with ARI, FRES, GFOG, FKGL, CL, SMOG and LW. The same study establishes why this must be its own verdict rather than folded into a quality reviewer, finding that 'quality and readability were largely independent dimensions' and that 'high-quality outputs do not necessarily have high readability'. arXiv:2406.12787 confirms leveled-text generation is a studied task whose outputs still require review, its manual pass finding 'misinformation introduction and inconsistent edit distribution' - so the band check constrains surface form only and does not certify content.
role_in_curriculum_builder: Restores the two gate-2 checks that prompt.md:193-195 already mandates but which appear in no unit_checks.json in this run. Runs at ARTIFACT_CONSISTENCY in policy/controller.v1.yaml, on the rendered document rather than on workers/lab.json, immediately after the Rendered Document Conformance Auditor and before any QA_* reviewer state.
issues_resolved: 'Readability/quality gates never ran. results/unit_checks.json for every lesson (L01-L04) contains only DOMAIN-SCHEMA-VALID, DOMAIN-VERIFIER, LAB-SCHEMA-VALID, RECEIPT-HASH-RESOLVES. No TEXT-READABILITY-BAND, no TEXT-BLOOM-VERBS, despite prompt.md naming both as mandatory gate-2 checks' (QA report, Critical). Also covers the High finding 'Vocabulary cap violated where prose exists at all' - L04 introduces mAVohm, 10A socket, mode dial and fuse against a declared cap of 2 new terms per lab.

function: Model reviewer that reads the rendered document as a learner-facing artifact and answers a fixed set of narrow, evidence-anchored yes/no probes drawn from inputs/unit_prose.v1.md - does the Explain section address the learner directly, is each new term defined at first use in the body text, does the unit teach one subject rather than a project, is the safety instruction stated in sentences a supervising adult can act on. Emits a per-probe verdict with the quoted supporting or offending text; code aggregates probes into the gate decision rather than the model returning a holistic score. Scoped strictly to what deterministic checks cannot decide.
what_makes_it_sota: Agents' Last Exam (arXiv:2606.05405) scores judged workflows 'not by general-purpose holistic prompts but by narrow, evidence-anchored yes/no probes whose answers code aggregates into the score', and reserves judging for what a deterministic alternative cannot cover. Braintrust (26 February 2026) draws the same boundary: 'LLM-as-a-judge should focus only on subjective dimensions that require language understanding. Separating deterministic checks from LLM-based scoring improves reliability.' The design point is that this reviewer is the second control for the rendering defect, never the first.
role_in_curriculum_builder: Reinstates REV-JUDGE-SINGLE-CROSS-FAMILY at the QA_COMMUNICATION state in policy/controller.v1.yaml, after ARTIFACT_CONSISTENCY and before QA_DECISION, reading document/<UNIT>.md rather than workers/lab.json. Its bypass must be recorded as a blocking divergence at FINAL_ACCEPTANCE rather than as an informational routing note.
issues_resolved: 'The one subjective quality check was bypassed identically on all 4 units' (QA report, Critical) - acceptance.json for L01-L04 records 'routing_divergence': 'USER_AUTHORIZED_IN_SESSION_MODEL; cross-family judge bypassed', leaving 'the pipeline's sole subjective gate inert for the entire run'. Also addresses the prose-contract violation the QA report names: 'unit_prose.v1.md mandates rendered prose ("Meet it... How it works... Scientifically honest at the learner's level"); this never happened.'

function: Deterministic auditor that runs last and refuses to let an acceptance record claim success on the basis of checks that did not execute. Reads the mandatory check inventory from prompt.md and policy/checks.v1.yaml, diffs it against the verdicts actually present in results/unit_checks.json and the run-level results directory, and rewrites the acceptance claim to enumerate executed, skipped, deferred and bypassed checks separately. Blocks ACCEPTED when any check mandated for the unit's gate has no recorded verdict, and downgrades any human-review status that has no recorded reviewer to an explicit unmet precondition.
what_makes_it_sota: Schema-level conformance is empirically a weak signal, so an acceptance decision computed from it alone is close to one that always passes: arXiv:2607.18261 measures '100% schema validity' alongside 'semantic success ... near 80%' and concludes 'structured output is a necessary interface layer, not a substitute for domain verification and fail-closed execution'; the Structured Output Benchmark (arXiv:2604.25359) finds 'near-perfect schema compliance' alongside a best value accuracy of '83.0% on text'. The fail-closed framing is the load-bearing one: a check with no verdict must read as not-passed, not as absent.
role_in_curriculum_builder: Runs at FINAL_ACCEPTANCE in policy/controller.v1.yaml, after PDF_VISUAL_QA and before the terminal_state is written, and owns the content of acceptance.json. It is the control that makes the other three agents non-bypassable, since each of them fails open today simply by not running.
issues_resolved: acceptance.json for all four units records 'claim': 'every executed automated check passed' with 'terminal_state': 'ACCEPTED' while the run was missing both mandated gate-2 TEXT-* checks entirely and had bypassed its only subjective judge. The QA report's root-cause assessment names the consequence: 'two independent gaps in the validation pipeline (missing gate-2 checks, bypassed judge) that mean schema validity was the only thing measured.' The documents' own 'Draft pending downstream human review' status (L01.md:3) likewise gates on nothing and is recorded nowhere.
